title: Probing the Trajectories of Reasoning Traces in Large Language Models
claim: A three-stage protocol generates reasoning traces, truncates them at fixed fractions, and reinjects the prefixes to probe how answers evolve.
layout: 3 rounded panels, left-to-right, progress-bar rows showing truncation deciles
description: A wide figure split into three rounded panels, read left to right, each with a numbered title. Panel 1, 'Generate Traces', stacks a gray System+Question box, a pink 'Model: Thinking enabled' box and a trace document icon joined by down arrows. Multipliers on the right (x4 datasets, x7 models, x3 runs) show the scale. Panel 2, 'Truncate Traces at Deciles', shows stacked trace cards with scissors above blue segmented bars for 0%, 20%, 50% and 100% of the trace. Panel 3, 'Reinject Traces & Probe', feeds System+Question, a blue Prefix and a Stopping Suffix into a pink 'Thinking disabled' model. A small table of alternative prefixes (original, random, trace-swap, shuffle) sits below it. A right-hand box shows a log-prob bar chart for multiple choice and the exact-answer judging procedure. Pink, blue and gray colour-code the model, prefix and prompt components.
caption: Overview of the trajectory-probing protocol. (1) Generate full responses and extract reasoning traces. (2) Truncate each reasoning trace at fixed token deciles, including an empty-prefix baseline and the complete trace. (3) Reinject each prefix with the original question and an early-stopping suffix, then measure final answer probability and correctness. For exact-answer tasks, answer correctness is judged by GPT-5 mini and we average the answer's token probabilities. Length-matched random, swapped, and shuffled prefixes provide control conditions. The main evaluation covers seven models, four benchmarks, and three runs; reasoning effort ablations are restricted to the gpt-oss models on GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly solve difficult problems by producing reasoning traces before emitting a final response. However, it remains unclear how accuracy and decision commitment evolve along a reasoning trajectory, and whether intermediate trace segments provide answer-relevant information beyond generic length or stylistic effects. Here, we propose a trajectory-probing protocol for evaluating how a reasoning model's predicted answer evolves along a partial reasoning trace. The protocol (1) generates a model's full reasoning trace, (2) truncates it at fixed token-percentiles, and (3) injects each partial trace back into the model, measuring the model's induced answer distribution. We apply the protocol to seven open-source reasoning models (Qwen3-4B/8B/14B, gpt-oss-20b/120b, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and Gemma-4-31B-it) across four benchmarks (GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro, Omni-MATH-2 and CompMath). The protocol reveals that accuracy and decision commitment generally increase as the percentage of provided reasoning tokens grows, and length, form, and token-identity controls confirm that gains stem from instance-specific semantic content rather than context length or generic reasoning style effects. Furthermore, cross-model probing shows that even stronger models frequently repeat the source model's errors when given its partial reasoning trace, while allowing further reasoning substantially improves recovery. Together, these results provide a reproducible, model-agnostic measurement of reasoning trace dynamics that generalizes across answer formats and can reveal model-specific failure modes invisible to aggregate accuracy.
